The mean-field terms are $H_{\text{Hartree}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{s, s'} \sum_{k_1, k_2} U(0) \langle c_s^\dagger(k_1) c_s(k_1) \rangle c_{s'}^\dagger(k_2) c_{s'}(k_2)$ $H_{\text{Fock}} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{s, s'} \sum_{k_1, k_2} U(k_1 - k_2) \langle c_s^\dagger(k_1) c_{s'}(k_1) \rangle c_{s'}^\dagger(k_2) c_s(k_2)$, where $U(k) = \sum_{n} U_n e^{-i k \cdot n}$ is the repulsive interaction strength ($U_n>0$) in the momentum basis. What are the possible order parameters that preserve translational symmetry for a Hartree-Fock mean-field Hamiltonian on a two-dimensional triangular lattice? Suppose you model a wavefunction of a quantum system with a recurrent neural network (RNN) out of which unbiased samples can be obtained. Within the framework of variational Monte Carlo, it is possible to estimate both the variational energy and the gradients of the energy with respect to the parameters $\lambda$ in the recurrent neural network wavefunction. The gradients of the energy are given by $\partial_{\lambda} E = \sum_{{\sigma},{\sigma'}} \partial_{\lambda} \left[ \psi^{*}_\lambda({\sigma}) H_{\sigma,\sigma'} \psi^{}_\lambda({\sigma'}) + \psi^{*}_\lambda({\sigma}) H_{\sigma,\sigma'} \partial_{\lambda} \psi^{}_\lambda({\sigma'})\right]$ A Monte Carlo estimator of the energy gradient is given by: $\partial_{\lambda} E \approx \frac{2}{N_S} \mathfrak{Re} \left ( \sum_{i=1}^{N_S} \frac{\partial_{\lambda}\psi^{*}_\lambda({\sigma^{(i)}})}{\psi^{*}_\lambda({\sigma^{(i)}})} E_{loc}({\sigma^{(i)}}) \right)$ where $N_s$ is the number of samples $\sigma^{(i)}$ drawn from the amplitude square of the RNN wavefunction. Which of the following statements is true: a. The gradient estimator is unbiased. b. The gradient estimator is biased because it misses a baseline involving the average energy. c. The gradient estimator is unbiased but has high variance. d. The gradient estimator is biased because in general the RNN and its gradients may have non-identical support in the computational basis. e. The gradient estimator is biased and has high variance. Return your answer in a $\boxed{}$ latex environment consisting of a list of the appropriate choices (a,b,c,d or e) separated by a ;. We want to build infinite two-dimensional tensor network wavefunction for a systems of spin-1 moments on square lattice interacting with SU(2)-symmetric interactions. We choose infinite projected entangled-pair state as the TN. We want to guarantee, that our TN respects i) translational symmetry of the lattice, ii) SU(2) symmetry of the interactions, and iii) symmetry of the lattice under rotations, C_4. A simplest choice is to generate the TN from a single 5-dimensional tensor $T_{puldr}$, with one physical index, $p$, corresponding to spin-1 physical degree of freedom and four virtual spaces V, labeled by indices $u$, $l$, $d$, and $r$, associated the up, left, down, and right directions on the lattice. We want tensor T to be invariant under the action of both spin-SU(2) and lattice rotations. Let's describe the action of SU(2) symmetry and lattice rotations: The SU(2) group acts on the tensors as $g(T) \rightarrow W(g)_{pp'} U(g)_{uu'} U(g)_{ll'} U(g)_{dd'} U(g)_{rr'} T_{p'u'l'd'r'} = T_{puldr}$ with U and W being appropriate matrix representations of SU(2) group. The group of lattice rotations acts on T by permutation (clockwise or anticlockwise) of its virtual indices, i.e. rotation by 90 degrees clockwise corresponds to $R(-\pi/2})(T_{puldr}) = T_{pruld}$. We choose the virtual spaces (indexed by u,l,d, and r) to be all identical and each composed from a direct sum of $V= 0 \oplus 1$ i.e. a direct sum of trivial irrep of SU(2) and spin-1 irrep of SU(2). How many (real-valued) variational parameters would our TN wavefunction have ? That is, how many independent tensors T_{puldr}, transforming under A irrep of the C_4 group of rotations and invariant under SU(2) group do we need to consider ?
